subject: psychology
title: Statistics & Methodology: Inferential Statistics
welcome_lead: Sign test, Mann-Whitney and Spearman — picking the right test.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology inferential statistics: choosing tests, significance, types of data.
final_note: Choosing the right test = data type + design + hypothesis.

concepts.def: Probability threshold below which result is unlikely by chance — typically p < 0.05.

walkthroughs.body_html: Decide three things: level of data (nominal/ordinal/interval), design (related/unrelated), aim (difference/correlation). Sign test: nominal, related. Mann-Whitney: ordinal, unrelated. Wilcoxon: ordinal, related. Chi-square: nominal, unrelated. Spearman's rho: ordinal correlation. Pearson's r: interval correlation.

Conventional threshold: p < 0.05 (5% chance result is due to chance). Type I error: false positive — reject true null. Type II error: false negative — accept false null. Stricter p < 0.01 reduces Type I but raises Type II.

Compare calculated statistic to critical value from tables. For most tests (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, sign) calculated must be less than or equal to critical. For chi-square and Spearman the calculated must be greater than or equal to. Always state direction of hypothesis (one-tailed vs two-tailed).
